messages.subject: Study design
parts:
Dear All,

I am planning a study design for a rare medium sized bird, found in tropical rainforest in SE Asia. The bird is rare and population is fragmented. 

Following the variable width line transect protocols is it required to walk transects both in the morning and evening?

And what proportion of the area needs to be sampled?

Would be really helpful if you can provide some suggestions

With best regards
Bhaskar

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Study design
parts:
Bhaskar

Strictly speaking, line transect sampling does not specify what time of day sampling should be performed.  This is a matter related to the biology of your study animal.  If the bird is readily seen/heard at one time of day, then that is the most efficient time of day to sample.

Likewise, distance sampling does not formulate the question of sampling effort in terms of proportion of study area to cover.   Rather, sampling effort is considered in terms of the number of replicate transects and number of animal detections.  When developing your sampling design, strive to have a reasonable number of transects (~20), placed in a systematically random manner, not following roads or tracks to provide spatial replication across your study area.  Furthermore, strive to produce ~60 detections of your study animal so you can do a credible job of estimating a detection function.

You can gain a sense of the total length of transects needed to produce your 60 detections if you have conducted a small pilot survey, noting the number of detections you make over a known length of transects. Follow the steps from this example (taken from Section 7.2.2.1 of Buckland et al. 2001, also in Section 2.4.2 of Buckland et al. (2015):
